abstract.p: In an (εs, εz)-weak non-interactive zero knowledge (NIZK), the soundness error is at most εs and the zero-knowledge error is at most εz. Goyal, Jain, and Sahai (CRYPTO 2019) stated that if εs + εz < 1 for some constants εs, εz, then (εs, εz)-weak NIZK can be turned into fullysecure NIZK, assuming sub-exponentially-secure public-key encryption. Later, however, they have discovered a gap in their proof. We revisit the problem of NIZK amplification:-We amplify NIZK arguments assuming only polynomially-secure public-key encryption, for any constants εs + εz < 1.-We amplify NIZK proofs assuming only one-way functions, for any constants εs + εz < 1.-When the soundness error εs is negligible to begin with, we can also amplify NIZK arguments assuming only one-way functions. Our results take a different route than that of Goyal, Jain, and Sahai. They are based on the hidden-bits paradigm, and can be viewed as a reduction from NIZK amplification to the better understood problem of pseudorandomness amplification.
